thread:
Maya: FYI — after the midnight key rotation the Okta→SCIM sync started failing for multiple customers. Provisioner logs show 'JWE decryption failed' and SCIM 502s. Anyone seen this pattern? :warning:

Dan: Seeing it too in infra traces. KMS audit shows some Decrypt failures and an alias swap around 00:01 UTC.

Alex: Which cert/key rotated? IdP cert or KMS envelope key?

Maya: We rotated the IdP client cert and also performed a scheduled KMS alias rotation for scim/envelope (per runbook). Stack snippet from the provisioner:

```
2024-03-15T00:02:11Z provisioner error: jwe: decrypt: rsa_oaep: decryption error
request_id=req_8f3b
```

Ellie: That rsa_oaep error smells like an asymmetric key being used where we expect a symmetric envelope key. The provisioner expects the KMS alias to point to a symmetric CMK for envelope unwrap.

Dan: Confirmed in KMS logs:
```
2024-03-15T00:01:50Z Decrypt Failed KeyId=arn:aws:kms:region:acct:key/abc123 Error=IncorrectKeyMaterial
```
Alias scim/envelope was remapped to a new key id that looks asymmetric (RSA) instead of the previous symmetric AES CMK.

Maya: Oof. That would cause the JWE decrypt path to fail. Do we have any RBAC changes that could have prevented the provisioner from calling KMS?

Ellie: No RBAC changes were pushed to prod during the window. Only the alias mapping update. However, our audit pipeline delayed KMS events by ~30s, so visibility was laggy.

Alex: Short-term mitigations: 1) remap alias back to prior symmetric key, 2) enable provisioner fallback (unwrapped path) behind a feature flag, 3) hold further alias rotations until compatibility check is added.

Maya: I'll create an incident and get approvals for emergency rollback. @Ellie can you confirm the previous key id and whether re-wrapping will leave any encrypted artifacts unreadable?

Ellie: Previous key id = key/xyz789 (symmetric). Any ciphertext re-encrypted under the new asymmetric key will be unreadable unless we rewrap with the symmetric key. But we rotated alias only — there was no mass re-encrypt job, so rolling back alias should restore decryptability for new envelopes.

Dan: Starting alias rollback now (will record in audit). PR: https://git.internal/infra/alias-rollbacks/PR-342 — applying infra-config change.

deploy-bot: alias-rollbacks/PR-342 merged and applied to infra-config (deploy started).

Alex: Pushed a quick feature-flagged fallback to canary to accept legacy unwrapped tokens while we verify. Canary tenants report provisioning success for 3/3 test tenants.

Maya: Monitoring shows SCIM success rate rising back to normal (~99.8%).

Dan: KMS Decrypt error count back to baseline after alias rollback. KMS audit shows Decrypt requests succeeding again.

Maya: Action items from incident:
- Dan: add a pre-rotate KMS compatibility check and block alias switch if key type mismatch.
- Alex: add a strict KID-to-alg mapping in provisioner and a clearer error that surfaces alias->key-type mismatch.
- Ellie: update runbook to require a 15m canary window and manual QA for alias rotations.
- Security (Maya): run audit for any failed decrypts that might indicate data loss or exposure.

Ellie: Postmortem summary (to be expanded): root cause = KMS alias update pointed to an asymmetric RSA key incompatible with our JWE envelope unwrap flow. Contributing factors = simultaneous IdP cert rotation + delayed KMS audit visibility.

Maya: Agreed. I'll draft the postmortem and add the runbook updates. Big takeaway: block automated alias swaps that change key material type, add KMS-compat checks in CI, and surface clearer errors in production logs. Thanks all :clap:

Alex: Also recommend a small regression test in staging that rotates alias to an intentionally incompatible key to validate detection.

Maya: Noted. I'll add that test to the pre-rotate checklist.
